title: Finnish translation: UnauthorizedError message and the login-request confirmation message
tech: Node/TypeScript backend only -- no new dependency, plain string literals
keyConstraints: Deliberately narrow follow-up from tasks 029/030/031: those three translation passes never touched backend/src/errors.ts, the zod validation schemas, or backend/src/middleware/rateLimit.ts, so several backend-originated strings are still English. Investigated every one of those and traced which are actually shown to a user versus dead/never-displayed text, and scoped this task to only the two that are genuinely visible -- do not expand scope to any other AppError subclass, validation message, or rate-limit message; that was a deliberate decision, not an oversight, confirmed with Ville. (1) UnauthorizedError (backend/src/errors.ts, clientMessage currently 'Unauthorized') is thrown from three call sites -- adminAuthService.ts's consumeLoginTokenAndCreateSession (invalid/expired/already-used login token) and requireMasseurAuth.ts's three guard checks (missing/invalid/expired session on every other admin API call). Traced the frontend consumers of each: AdminLoginCallback.tsx's catch block (`error instanceof ApiError ? error.message : ...`) DOES render UnauthorizedError's message directly -- so the login-token-exchange call site is genuinely user-visible (a masseur who reuses a link or waits past the 15-minute TTL sees this). By contrast, every other admin page's 401 handler (AdminDashboard.tsx line ~50, and the same pattern in AdminCalendar.tsx/AdminAvailability.tsx/AdminServices.tsx) calls onSessionEnded() and silently redirects to login WITHOUT ever reading error.message -- so requireMasseurAuth.ts's three throw sites never surface this string to a user today. Translate UnauthorizedError's single clientMessage string once in errors.ts (e.g. to something like 'Ei valtuutusta' or a more natural equivalent -- Ville should review for naturalness) -- since all call sites share the one class, this automatically covers the visible path without needing to special-case call sites or split the error into variants; that would be needless complexity for a single shared 401. (2) GENERIC_LOGIN_REQUEST_MESSAGE in backend/src/routes/auth.ts ('If that email is registered, a login link has been sent.') is returned by POST /auth/login-request and rendered verbatim by AdminLoginRequest.tsx (confirmed: resultMessage state is set directly from response.message and displayed with no fallback/rewrite) on every successful submission -- always visible, not an edge case. Translate this string in place; preserve the existing security property documented at its definition (identical response regardless of whether the submitted email matches ADMIN_EMAIL -- never branch this message on that outcome) exactly as-is, only the language changes. Out of scope, confirmed with Ville and left English deliberately: every other AppError subclass (ValidationError, ServiceNotFoundError, SlotUnavailableError, BookingNotFoundError, BookingNotPendingError, BookingNotConfirmedError, BookingNotModifiableError, AvailabilityRuleNotFoundError, AvailabilityExceptionNotFoundError), all zod validation .message strings across the route/validation files, the 'Logged out' string in auth.ts (also traced -- AdminDashboard.tsx's handleLogout awaits logout() but never reads the response body), and all rateLimit.ts messages.
description: Translate the two backend-originated strings that are actually shown to the masseur in English today: the UnauthorizedError message (visible when a login link is invalid, expired, or already used) and the login-request confirmation message (visible every time the masseur requests a login link). Both are currently the only user-visible gaps left over from the three prior Finnish-translation tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: UnauthorizedError's clientMessage in backend/src/errors.ts is natural Finnish

GENERIC_LOGIN_REQUEST_MESSAGE in backend/src/routes/auth.ts is natural Finnish, and the existing security property (identical response text regardless of whether the email matched ADMIN_EMAIL) is unchanged -- only the language of the string changes
No other AppError subclass, validation message, or rateLimit.ts message is touched -- this is intentionally out of scope

backend/test/unit/adminAuthService.test.ts, backend/test/unit/requireMasseurAuth.test.ts, and any other backend test asserting on the literal English 'Unauthorized' or 'If that email is registered...' strings are deliberately updated to the new Finnish text, with each assertion's intent re-checked (not blind find-and-replace)
frontend/test/AdminLoginCallback.test.tsx and frontend/test/AdminLoginRequest.test.tsx (and any other frontend test asserting on these two specific strings) are updated to match
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/
securityConsiderations: GENERIC_LOGIN_REQUEST_MESSAGE's existing anti-enumeration property (response is identical whether or not the submitted email matches ADMIN_EMAIL) must be preserved exactly -- only translate the string, never make it conditional on requestLoginLink's outcome.
